clue.text: Olympic host city (US): gamble on Klammer's lead over mountain backfired?

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the US city

indicators.note: something that backfired went the wrong way, so this group of letters is read backwards
the skier's initial is put on after the gamble word before the whole lot turns round
in the reversed reading the gamble word sits over and around the mountain, enclosing it

parts.note: to dice is to gamble
an alp is a mountain

indicators.note: the lead of Klammer's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clue about a winter Olympics town, with Austrian downhill legend Franz Klammer taking a gamble on a mountain that goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfired' turns DICALPE + K into KEPLACID, which follows LA. 'Olympic host' is the definition; '(US)' just tags LA as an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Placid in New York State staged the Winter Olympics in 1932 and 1980, so it has played Olympic host.

clue.text: European driver, inexperienced adult, double parking

indicators.note: double here tells us the parking letter is written a second time straight after the first

parts.note: an inexperienced driver is a learner, L on the plates
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A learner driver from Europe double-parks, as beginners might.
explanation.walkthrough: double doubles the parking letter, giving PP after L and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lapp is one of the Sami people of northern Scandinavia, so a European.

clue.text: Have the expertise to tell Welsh and Spanish apart?

definitions.text: Have the expertise to tell Welsh and Spanish apart?

parts.words: Have the expertise to tell Welsh and Spanish apart?
parts.note: Welsh and Spanish are both kinds of onion bulb, so telling them apart literally is the idiom for being an expert

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about distinguishing two languages or peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh and Spanish read as nationalities or languages, but here they are varieties of onion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be knowledgeable and competent in a subject, which is having the expertise.

clue.text: Supplier of hot meal or, post-prandially, the father of the bride?

definitions.meaning: a kitchen appliance whose slices spring up hot, supplying toast as a meal

definitions.text: post-prandially, the father of the bride?
definitions.meaning: after the wedding meal, the bride's father pops up to propose a toast

explanation.surface: Asks what serves hot food, or what the bride's father does after dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot meal' is toast; at the reception the father stands up after eating and raises a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: The appliance ejects browned bread; the speaker rises abruptly and proposes a toast, so both are things that spring up and give toasts.

clue.text: Group spotted in the North Atlantic when rowers shouted out

definitions.text: Group spotted in the North Atlantic

indicators.note: something shouted out is heard spoken, so these words count by their sound

parts.note: when means as, and rowers are oars, giving 'as oars'

explanation.surface: Something seen in the North Atlantic as a crew yell out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as oars' said aloud sounds like the island name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Azores are a Portuguese archipelago, a group of islands in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Here's Joe, very short of runs in India, dismissed short of ton

indicators.note: short of ton means the letter for ton is dropped at the end
the soldier and trimmed word go in among India and the dismissal word

parts.note: India is I in the radio alphabet
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
GI Joe, the American soldier

indicators.note: very short of runs means the word very loses its R

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket report: Joe, in India, is out just short of a century.
explanation.walkthrough: GIVEY goes inside I...OUT to make IGIVEYOUT; 'short of ton' then drops the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are spoken when presenting someone or proposing a toast, as in 'Ladies and gentlemen, here's the bride'.

clue.text: Shut crystal box

definitions.meaning: an old word for fastening a door with a bar
... is a crystalline mineral, as in Iceland ...

explanation.surface: Close up a box made of crystal.
explanation.definitionFit: Three separate senses of one word: bolting shut, a lustrous mineral, and boxing practice.

clue.text: What links Southgate to Arsenal — training ground in idyllic place

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, and training means being shaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seems to be about football: England manager Gareth Southgate and Arsenal at a lovely training ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Southgate and Arsenal are London Underground stations, not a manager and a club.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Underground line running through north London connects these two stations, so it links them.

clue.text: Lure agitated herd astray

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: going astray is erring

explanation.surface: A decoy disturbs a herd and sends it wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a false clue meant to lead astray, a lure or decoy.

clue.text: Big pubs around Cairo busted by officers detecting chemical compound

indicators.note: the police letters come beside what precedes them
the two pubs sit around the size abbreviation

parts.note: PH is a map abbreviation for public house, two of them for pubs
OS is outsize, big

indicators.note: busted means broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, are detecting officers

explanation.surface: Large bars near Cairo are raided by detectives looking for a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphoric acid, H3PO4, is a substance made of several elements, so a chemical compound.

clue.text: See 9
Not making final track listing unpublishable?

definitions.meaning: a song left off the final album is not on the record
a remark made ... must not be published

explanation.surface: A song dropped from an album is a kind of secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidential remark given to a journalist may not be printed, while a song cut from an album never appears on the disc.

clue.text: Pie, counterintuitively, for each working cafe — OK?

parts.note: apiece means for each

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cafe owner checks whether pie at so much each is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy as pie' and the answer both mean easy, though a pie is not cake: hence 'counterintuitively'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie as in 'easy as pie' is something simple, and so is the idiom for an easy task.

clue.text: Arty festivities Defoe did a different way on either side of street

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go on both sides of the street abbreviation
done a different way means the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Daniel Defoe stages artistic celebrations in a fresh way along a street.
explanation.definitionFit: An eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music, poetry and arts, so arty festivities.

clue.text: See 2
Detective Sergeant so pressed for attachment to Feds?

parts.note: Detective Sergeant is DS; put the chemical symbol for iron in front, as the answer says, and it turns into the Feds the clue ends with

explanation.surface: A detective sergeant flattered into joining the American federal agents.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, Fe (iron) on DS, and it makes FEDS. The definition is woven into that instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron-on patch or transfer is fixed to fabric by pressing it with a hot iron.

clue.text: Better liquor at this location in Bavaria?

parts.note: wort is the liquor from malt that is fermented into beer
hier is German for here

explanation.surface: Asks whether the beer here in Bavaria is superior.
explanation.definitionFit: More deserving or more estimable, a comparative like better in the sense of more worthy.

clue.text: 'Coxa' — the place to hang out!

definitions.meaning: coxa is the anatomical Latin for the hip

explanation.surface: Coxa sounds like the name of a fashionable bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Coxa is the medical term for the hip and its socket; a fashionable spot is a hip joint.

clue.text: At barbie, Jack becomes mine

parts.note: to turn is to become, as milk turns sour
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: At a barbecue, a man called Jack decides something belongs to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barbie' is Australian slang for a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit was a jack, a person or device that turned meat on a spit over a fire.

clue.text: Legendary source of magic flier

explanation.surface: A mythical bird that grants magic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian wizard is a legendary magician, and a small falcon shares his name.

clue.text: Deutsche Messe's sequence arrangement

indicators.note: the answer is a sequence of letters running across these words

explanation.surface: The order of service of a German Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Deutsche Messe is German for 'German Mass', as set by Schubert.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a plan or systematic layout, as in colour scheme, so an arrangement.

clue.text: Private and seaman in double act, ditching uniform and tux

indicators.note: the two words go in the double act
ditching means throwing away, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a duet is a double act
U is uniform in the radio alphabet
private means inner, as in inner thoughts
Jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A soldier and a sailor perform as a duo, changing out of uniform into evening dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Tux, short for tuxedo, is American for the formal black jacket worn at evening events.

clue.text: See 7
Partook of fine, rounded cheese

indicators.note: rounded means turned round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: partook of food means ate
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone ate a good, round cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek cheese, made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: So Scrooge was 'spirited' on occasion?

definitions.meaning: Scrooge was whisked by ghosts from one time to another, past, present and future
the idiom means now and then, occasionally

explanation.surface: Asks whether Scrooge was occasionally lively.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's A Christmas Carol the ghosts carry Scrooge to Christmases past, present and yet to come.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means occasionally, now and again, as does 'on occasion'.

clue.text: See 24
Dad is had with this bribe

parts.note: split the answer 1-2-1 and it reads as an instruction to swap the first letter of dad for the eighth letter of the alphabet, making had

explanation.surface: A father is conned by a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer as 'D as H', an instruction that turns DAD into HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash is West African English for a tip or bribe, a gift given to grease the wheels.

clue.text: Saint, being otherworldly, heralded with pizzazz

parts.note: ET, the film's extra-terrestrial, is an otherworldly being

indicators.note: with pizzazz means with flamboyant energy, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A saint of unearthly character is announced with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Etheldreda, or Audrey, was a seventh-century Anglo-Saxon abbess of Ely, venerated as a saint.
